item.research_question: How does the CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy behave under plane-stress deformation (biaxial bulging) at cryogenic temperatures, and what are the underlying microstructural mechanisms?
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction arc melting followed by homogenization annealing at 1200 °C for 24 h; hot extrusion at 950 °C with a speed of 15 mm/s and ratio of 3.01; final annealing at 950 °C for 1 h to produce thin-walled tubes; tubes cut and flattened into circular sheets (42 mm diameter) for testing.
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at −160 °C and −196 °C; isothermal bulging tests at −190 °C, −140 °C, and room temperature (RT) with bulging ratios of 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%; punch diameter 36 mm; minimum achievable temperature −190 °C with 1 °C accuracy.
key_findings: At −196 °C, ultimate tensile strength exceeds 2100 MPa and elongation is higher than 70%.
At −160 °C, yield strength exceeds 500 MPa, ultimate tensile strength is near 1700 MPa, and elongation is approximately 60%.
Ultimate bulging heights at splitting were 12 mm for both −190 °C and −140 °C.
At −190 °C, the maximum thinning rate was 6.32%, 4.52%, 12.56%, and 10.74% smaller than at −140 °C for bulging ratios of 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%, respectively.
Specimens with a bulging ratio of 25% showed the best thickness uniformity at both −190 °C and −140 °C.
The ratio of small-angle grain boundaries increased from 8.6% to 53.6% as the bulging ratio increased from 25% to 100% at −190 °C.
Average grain diameter in the original state was 8.85 μm, decreasing minimally after deformation (e.g., 8.28 μm at −190 °C).
The ratio of small-angle grain boundaries at 100% bulging ratio was 53.3% at RT, 45.9% at −140 °C, and 53.6% at −190 °C.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the simultaneous increase in strength and ductility at cryogenic temperatures is due to the appearance of nanoscale twinning, which postpones the onset of necking. For biaxial deformation, dislocation motion is identified as a main mechanism, evidenced by the significant increase in small-angle grain boundaries with increasing bulging ratio, while nanoscale twinning (difficult to observe with EBSD) may be enhanced at lower temperatures to improve plasticity.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: Both the strength and the ductility improves as the temperature decreases from −160 °C to −196 °C.

The appearance of nanoscale twinning may postpone the onset of necking, which may be the reason for the increase in both the strength and the ductility as the temperature decreases from −160 °C to −196 °C.

It may be obtained that as the temperature decreases from RT to −196 °C, the effect of the dislocation motion of the biaxial deformation is not weakened, while the effect of the nanoscale twinning, which is difficult to be observed with EBSD, may be enhanced and may be the cause of the improvement in the plasticity of the CoCrFeMnNi HEA at cryogenic temperatures.
